title: Chloe Is Hiring
brand: built by I.Magin · draft for Chloe
headline: A design company is hiring. You'd never find it on a job board.
subhead: This is the page you send to somebody good instead of posting into a pile of five hundred applicants. It is already built — every blank on it is a question only Chloe can answer.

sections.heading: The work
items: Hero — the best piece the studio has shipped

sections.heading: Why a page beats a posting
items: A job posting puts a small studio in a queue behind every company with a recruiting budget, and buys back a stack of applicants who applied to two hundred other places the same afternoon.

A link does the opposite. You text it to the one person you already have in mind, or hand it to someone at an event, and they see the actual work, the actual terms, and a way to reply — in about twenty seconds, on their phone, before the moment passes.
Nothing on this page claims anything about the studio. The role, the terms and the pay are Chloe's to fill, and until she does they stay visibly blank.

items.name: This page, finished and live
items.note: One page, real work, real terms, a link she can text to a candidate today.

items.name: The full setup
items.note: A proper studio site with the portfolio, a contact form that reaches her phone, and Google, Instagram and Facebook set up to match.

items.name: Kept current
items.note: New work posted as it ships, roles opened and closed as they change. Cancel any month.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.title: Six answers and it's live today.
sections.note: Position, hours, where, start, pay range, deadline — plus four or five images of the work. That is the whole brief. Nothing goes public under her studio's name until she says yes.

footer_notes: This is an unpublished draft made to show Chloe what her hiring page would look like. It makes no claim about her studio, its work, its terms or its pay.
